[Bush's Pasture Park](/wiki/Bush%27s_Pasture_Park "Bush's Pasture Park"), a 90.5-acre (36.6 ha) urban park a few blocks south of downtown Salem, features natural groves of native [Oregon White Oak](/wiki/Garry_Oak "Garry Oak") trees, the historic Bush House, a rose garden, and adjacent Deepwood Estates.[[69]](#cite_note-69)

Methionine biosynthesis

As an essential amino acid, methionine is not synthesized [*de novo*](/wiki/De_novo_synthesis "De novo synthesis") in humans and other animals, which must ingest methionine or methionine-containing proteins. In plants and microorganisms, methionine biosynthesis belongs to the [aspartate](/wiki/Aspartate "Aspartate") family, along with threonine and [lysine](/wiki/Lysine "Lysine") (via [diaminopimelate](/wiki/Diaminopimelate "Diaminopimelate"), but not via [α-aminoadipate](/wiki/Alpha-Aminoadipic_acid "Alpha-Aminoadipic acid")). The main backbone is derived from [aspartic acid](/wiki/Aspartic_acid "Aspartic acid"), while the sulfur may come from [cysteine](/wiki/Cysteine "Cysteine"), [methanethiol](/wiki/Methanethiol "Methanethiol"), or [hydrogen sulfide](/wiki/Hydrogen_sulfide "Hydrogen sulfide").[[9]](#cite_note-review-9)

* First, aspartic acid is converted via β-aspartyl semialdehyde into [homoserine](/wiki/Homoserine "Homoserine") by two reduction steps of the terminal carboxyl group (homoserine has therefore a γ-hydroxyl, hence the [homo-](/wiki/Homologous_series "Homologous series") series). The intermediate aspartate semialdehyde is the branching point with the lysine biosynthetic pathway, where it is instead [condensed](/wiki/Aldol_condensation "Aldol condensation") with pyruvate. Homoserine is the branching point with the threonine pathway, where instead it is isomerised after activating the terminal hydroxyl with phosphate (also used for methionine biosynthesis in plants).[[9]](#cite_note-review-9)
* Homoserine is then activated with a phosphate, succinyl or an acetyl group on the hydroxyl.
